title: 250 Lincoln Road affordable housing plan advances
subtitle: Erbsville Road subdivision public meeting, library update, winter events and a Woolwich Street widening by-law.
overview: Council approved a staff report on 250 Lincoln Road, the former church site the City bought for affordable housing {{vote:m1}}. Staff will start planning and procurement work, consult the public, housing providers and community organizations, demolish the existing building in spring 2026, and consider temporary green space once it is gone.

The site is close to Lincoln Heights Public School, whose parking lot is used for drop-off and pickup. Delegates raised concerns about school traffic and safety, possible zoning changes, the timing of demolition and the housing targets behind the plan. Staff said no zoning change was approved. Any amendment would return to Council with further public meetings.

Earlier, an informal public meeting on two subdivision applications on Erbsville Road took place. No decision was made, and staff will report back. Council also received a library update and passed a by-law widening Woolwich Street {{vote:m2}}. Members noted Winterloo, a food bank fundraiser that raised $8,000, and a $17.8 million provincial expansion of St. David's Catholic Secondary School.

decisions.detail: Council approved report CAO2026-003 and directed staff to proceed with planning and procurement for affordable housing on the site, following the actions and timelines in the report.
Council directed staff to engage the public, affordable housing providers and community organizations to inform changes to the planning framework and the Request for Expressions of Interest.
Council directed staff to demolish the existing structure at 250 Lincoln Road in spring 2026 to make way for development.
Council directed staff to consider using the site as publicly accessible green space after demolition.

debate: Staff said the site was bought with funds set aside for affordable housing. They proposed a quick timeline but said it could be extended to draw better submissions. They would return to Council if the responses were not satisfactory.

A school council delegate described traffic congestion and gaps in safe walking routes around Lincoln Heights Public School. The delegate asked that parking and sidewalks be kept open during demolition and construction. Staff said they would keep the sidewalk clear and write contract language to avoid work at pickup and drop-off times.

Two delegates asked Council to postpone or change the report. They cited slowing population growth, the risk of demolishing before a development partner is chosen, and a wish to keep low-density zoning on the site. Staff said any zoning amendment would go through the standard planning process with public meetings. Councillors said the report did not approve a zoning change.

Some councillors said the site was bought to deliver affordable housing and that the proposals should not be limited too early. Others stressed balancing neighbourhood context, school safety and a possible community space with broader housing need.

At the Erbsville Road public meeting, a resident raised concerns about runoff in a swale, an unclear property line and loss of a tree line. Councillors asked about buffers to the environmentally sensitive area, groundwater recharge, wetlands and a possible trail connection.
